audit_status.source_base: ChatGPT-authored Psalms completion draft using public-domain KJV as familiar alignment scaffold with curated Hebrew/textual overrides; full WLC/OSHB/source-witness audit pending
audit_status.review_note: Refuge, Most High, divine protection, plague, angels/messengers, danger, and trust.

verses.restored: Whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High will lodge in the shadow of the Almighty.

familiar.text: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.

notes.title: Protection poetry
notes.body: Psalm 91 speaks in sweeping poetry about divine refuge. It should not be turned into a guarantee that faithful people will never be injured, infected, traumatized, persecuted, or killed, nor used to blame people when harm occurs.

verses.restored: I will say of YHWH, “My refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust.”

familiar.text: I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.

verses.restored: Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence.

familiar.text: Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence.

verses.restored: He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and shield.

familiar.text: He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.

verses.restored: Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day;

familiar.text: Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day;

verses.restored: Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.

familiar.text: Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.

verses.restored: A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee.

familiar.text: A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee.

verses.restored: Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.

familiar.text: Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.

verses.restored: Because thou hast made YHWH, which is my refuge, even the most High, thy habitation;

familiar.text: Because thou hast made the LORD, which is my refuge, even the most High, thy habitation;

verses.restored: There shall no evil befall thee, neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling.

familiar.text: There shall no evil befall thee, neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling.

verses.restored: For he will command his messengers concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.

familiar.text: For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.

notes.title: Messengers / angels
notes.body: Hebrew malakhim means messengers and is commonly rendered angels here. Matthew 4 and Luke 4 later quote verses 11–12 in the temptation narrative; that reception does not make the psalm a license for reckless testing of divine protection.

verses.restored: They will lift you up in their hands, lest you strike your foot against a stone.

familiar.text: They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.

verses.restored: Thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder: the young lion and the dragon shalt thou trample under feet.

familiar.text: Thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder: the young lion and the dragon shalt thou trample under feet.

verses.restored: Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name.

familiar.text: Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name.

verses.restored: He shall call upon me, and I will answer him: I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honour him.

familiar.text: He shall call upon me, and I will answer him: I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honour him.

verses.restored: With long life will I satisfy him, and show him my salvation.

familiar.text: With long life will I satisfy him, and shew him my salvation.

translation_notes: This chapter completes corpus coverage as a ChatGPT-authored draft. KJV is retained as a familiar comparison layer; a separate automated reference pass adds BSB and pointed Hebrew without replacing the restored draft.
safety_note: Protection language is poetry of trust, not a guarantee of immunity from illness, accident, violence, or death; never blame harmed people for insufficient faith.
source_witness_audit_flags: Compare directly with WLC/OSHB, Septuagint, Dead Sea Psalms witnesses where extant, and other textual witnesses during the global audit. Preserve poetic parallelism, superscriptions, acrostic structure, duplicate/reused psalms, and significant Hebrew/Greek divergences rather than harmonizing them.
